name: Filgrastim
route_note: daily SC injection or IV infusion until neutrophil recovery
originator: Amgen with Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center
owner: Amgen (Neupogen); biosimilars (Sandoz, Pfizer, Teva and others)

discovery.by: Lawrence Souza (Amgen) with Karl Welte and Malcolm Moore (Memorial Sloan Kettering)
discovery.note: Human G-CSF was purified from a bladder carcinoma cell line and its gene cloned; the recombinant protein is made in E. coli.

tagline: Recombinant G-CSF that shortens neutropenia after chemotherapy
summary: Filgrastim is a non-glycosylated recombinant human granulocyte colony-stimulating factor produced in E. coli. It stimulates neutrophil production and release, reducing febrile neutropenia after myelosuppressive chemotherapy and mobilising stem cells for collection. It was the subject of the first US biosimilar approval.
mechanism: G-CSF binds the G-CSF receptor (CSF3R) on myeloid progenitors and neutrophils, activating JAK–STAT signalling that drives proliferation, differentiation and survival of the neutrophil lineage and enhances neutrophil function.
Filgrastim also loosens retention of haematopoietic stem cells in the marrow (partly by protease-mediated cleavage of CXCL12–CXCR4 interactions), mobilising CD34+ cells into blood for apheresis.
uses: Reduction of febrile neutropenia with myelosuppressive chemotherapy
Acute myeloid leukaemia after induction or consolidation
Haematopoietic syndrome of acute radiation syndrome

history.title: Gene cloned
history.detail: Amgen and Memorial Sloan Kettering researchers clone human G-CSF.

history.title: Severe chronic neutropenia
history.detail: Approval extended to congenital, cyclic and idiopathic neutropenia.

history.title: EU biosimilars
history.detail: First filgrastim biosimilars authorised in the EU.

history.title: First US biosimilar
history.detail: Zarxio (filgrastim-sndz, Sandoz) becomes the first biosimilar approved under the US BPCI Act.

history.title: Radiation syndrome
history.detail: FDA approves filgrastim for haematopoietic acute radiation syndrome under the Animal Rule.

pk.bioavailability: SC absorption reaches peak in 2–8 hours

facts: Zarxio was the first biosimilar approved in the United States, in March 2015.
